name: CA-23
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+9 district lean favors incumbent Obernolte
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The district's Republican lean, Obernolte's incumbency, and his dominant fundraising advantage over a barely funded challenger all point to a comfortable Republican hold, and prediction markets agree at roughly 95% Republican. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays close to the district baseline.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or a polling surprise showing Obernolte under 50% would be the main signals of a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican incumbent Jay Obernolte seeks another term in this Republican-leaning California district, where the partisan baseline favors his party by about nine points. He advanced to the general election and faces Democrat Tessa Lynn Hodge, a first-time challenger with minimal resources.

The financial picture is lopsided: Obernolte has raised about $1.5 million and holds $1.6 million on hand, while Hodge has raised under $80,000 with roughly $10,000 remaining. Outside groups have spent little on either side. No public polls cover the race, and prediction markets give Democrats only about a 6% chance. Absent contrary evidence, Obernolte is a clear favorite, though the lack of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
